parsed.explanation: Combined operative regime: the national passport regime is in force (Supreme Court allowed sex-marker restrictions in November 2025), so a visitor's home-passport sex marker can be blocked or confiscated at processing, with documented stranding. Entry refusal for discrepant documents is cable-mandated, and fraud ineligibility is possible. Facility bans cover 19 states plus one unit, with criminal trespass in four and one documented arrest followed by 24 hours in a men's ward. Documented custody harms include conversion-style policies, forced labour and severe sexual abuse in immigration custody, and the corrections bureau has stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers. Counterterrorism language targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups. Partial offsets are injunctions, pending litigation, a federal hate-crimes statute, nondiscrimination in 22 states plus DC, and no death penalty. Violence figures lack denominators and are not weighed. The travelling-minor exposure is higher.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport sex-marker restrictions in force since the November 2025 ruling. Trans and nonbinary travellers report passports confiscated or blocked, with some stranded. The 2025 cable requires refusal where documents are discrepant, and fraud ineligibility is possible.
entry_documents.protection: Civil-liberties suit pending for seven plaintiffs. Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry. Fraud ineligibility is not automatic and has waiver options.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can move to refusal, questioning and stranding abroad. Foreign governments' advisories add friction for onward travel.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: One documented arrest for trespass in a women's restroom, handcuffed and held 24 hours in the men's ward. Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men. Federal corrections adopted conversion-style policies and stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Pretrial release was granted in the arrest case. Some federal orders are enjoined.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility rules in government buildings can convert a bathroom encounter into arrest and birth-sex custody placement. Federal custody policies apply to any detained trans traveller.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility bans in government buildings in 19 states plus one unit. Bans reach private settings in 6 states. Criminal trespass applies in 4 states. Visitors have no exemption from state-level rules.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Most states (29 plus 4 units plus DC) have no mapped ban. Some bans are enjoined or in litigation.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State facility bans operate alongside federal entry and custody rules. The effect is that a single encounter can cross sovereign levels.

care_services.exposure: The state bans licensed professionals from hormone therapy or surgery for minors. A regional hospital cancelled all gender-affirming surgery in February 2025, including for an adult. Federal subpoenas seek minors' records, and federal funding restrictions apply.
care_services.protection: A 2023 public-employee plan settlement covers medically necessary care for employees and dependants and may extend to care for minors outside the state. Hospital cancellation is not confirmed as permanent.
care_services.interaction: Adult surgical access can contract through funding decisions made outside the state. A travelling minor's care is constrained by state law and federal funding rules.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: The December 2025 reward memo and May 2026 counterterrorism strategy frame 'radically pro-transgender' groups as targets for neutralisation. The 2025 orders direct criminal prosecution of teachers for social transition support.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The strategy says counterterrorism will not target people who only disagree. Several orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing can raise scrutiny of trans advocates, though the direct effect on visitors is unclear.

minors_guardians.exposure: A travelling minor cannot receive lawful transition care from a state-licensed clinician. Federal prosecution exposure applies to school staff who use a trans minor's preferred name. A guardian can face questions around minors' records and care.
minors_guardians.protection: The public-employee plan may pay for minors' care obtained outside the state. Some federal orders are enjoined.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian with a covered plan has a payment route that the state cannot deliver locally.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police investigated three violent crimes against trans women in one major city in 2023. Recorded killing rates are floor counts without a denominator, so they are not weighed as trans-specific risk.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police publicly acknowledged the violence and opened investigations. Hate-crime statute applies nationally, but only 23 states cover gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence has not been shown above background rates. Outcomes of the investigations are not recorded.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Federal and state remedies are slow or contested. Many orders are unresolved. The outcome of the 2023 minors-ban litigation is unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined several federal orders. Nondiscrimination covers 22 states plus DC. Same-sex marriage is recognised nationally, though this is general LGB rather than trans-specific.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Court remedies partly reduce exposure but do not reverse documented passport, facility and custody practices in force.

anchor_checks.comparison: Closest match. Both have birth-sex custody with documented assaults and arrests under a cross-dressing-type rule, and no execution. This case is somewhat more severe because of documented sexual abuse and forced labour in immigration custody, and the national passport block at entry. It is somewhat less severe than the anchor's reported multi-year custody patterns, since no capital or prolonged-custody cases are documented.

This case is lower. The anchor's universal register with almost no appeals is a single exclusion mechanism, while here passport blocking is in force but challenged in court and has some injunctions. There is no documented custody harm in the anchor, so this case carries additional severity from custody abuse and placement.

Similar. Both involve document-matching checks at entry, raids or arrests, and birth-sex facility rules. This case has more documented custody sexual abuse and stronger federal hostility. It has somewhat better partial remedies through court injunctions and a national hate-crime statute.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets a national passport regime that can block a discrepant sex marker at entry and a state patchwork of facility bans with arrest exposure. A detention that begins with a bathroom or document issue can lead to birth-sex custody and documented abuse, with federal and state layers interacting. Care and minor-related rules narrow access for travelling families. Courts and injunctions give partial, unpredictable relief, and nondiscrimination and hate-crime protections operate in a minority of jurisdictions. Violence is undocumented on a trans-specific basis. Overall this is high risk, at the upper edge of the band, but not at the capital tier.
